subject: Energy
title: Industrial Electrification
description: A short lesson to help you apply Industrial Electrification.

hook.text: Industry burns fossil fuels for extreme heat—cement kilns, steel furnaces, and chemical plants need 500–1,500°C.

buildup.text: Electric arc furnaces already produce 30% of global steel—using electricity to melt scrap metal at high temperatures.

discovery.text: Industrial heat pumps can now reach 200°C—suitable for food processing, paper, and chemical drying applications.

twist.text: For temperatures above 500°C, green hydrogen or electric resistance heating may replace gas—but costs remain higher.

climax.text: Electrifying industry could cut 25% of global CO₂—but requires massive grid expansion and very cheap clean power.

punchline.text: Electric heat for factories—the hardest decarbonization frontier.

quiz.question: What percentage of global steel do electric arc furnaces already produce?
